name: altair
label: Altair (alpha Aql, A7 Vn, rapid rotator)

sources: Monnier et al. 2007: equatorial 3.67 / polar 2.96 mas, rotation axis at PA -61.8 deg
notes: Major axis (the equator) at PA 28.2 deg E of N.

sources: Monnier et al. 2007, Science 317, 342 (CHARA/MIRC imaging, beta free): polar radius 1.634 Rsun = 1.479 mas angular radius, equatorial 2.029 Rsun = 1.835 mas (diameters 2.96 and 3.67 mas, axis ratio 1.24); inclination 57.2 +/- 1.9 deg; rotation-axis position angle -61.8 +/- 0.8 deg E of N; T_pol 8450, T_eq 6860 K; omega/omega_crit 0.923; v sin i 240 km/s
van Belle et al. 2001, ApJ 559, 1155 (PTI): ellipse 3.461 x 3.037 mas, axis ratio 1.14
van Leeuwen 2007: parallax 194.95 +/- 0.57 mas (5.13 pc); Ducati 2002: V 0.76; H, K ~0.1 (approximate)
notes: theta_ld_mas 3.296 = sqrt(3.67 x 2.96), the equal-area diameter of the Monnier 2007 ellipse; the `ellipse` block carries the shape (major axis along PA 28.2 deg = rotation axis -61.8 + 90).
Gravity darkening (the pole 1600 K hotter than the equator) is NOT modelled: hbtsim's ellipse is an affine, uniformly limb-darkened disk, so the real |V|^2 asymmetry differs in detail.
First null of the equal-area disk at 650 nm: 49.6 m; the oblateness campaigns use the ISI triangle with 30 m sides.
Anchors are Vega magnitudes converted with the band table's Vega -> AB offsets (V +0.02, H +1.39, K +1.85).
The radius is derived from theta_LD and the distance.
assumptions: star.ld_table (A-type law of beta Aur at 9300 K; Altair is 7500 K)
ellipse (uniform-brightness affine disk; no gravity darkening)
